title: Interactive competitor scenario deck and decision anchors for model procurement
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Create an interactive scenario deck and a concise set of decision anchors that the GTM, SRE, and Procurement teams can use to evaluate new model vendors and open-model variants. The artifact will translate benchmarking signals (latency, p95 tail, unit cost, quantization compatibility, licensing risk) into tactical procurement triggers and runbooks for: (1) pilot qualification, (2) canary rollouts, and (3) fallback orchestration.

Scope: collate benchmarking data sources, synthesize 6 competitive scenarios (fast cheap models, high-latency high-accuracy models, regional supply disruptions, quantization incompatibility, license change shock, multi-model hybrid routing), and produce both an interactive slide deck and a one-page decision anchor for exec review. Deliverables include the scenario deck, a csv of normalized benchmarking features, a short checklist for pilots, and recommended experiment definitions for the engineering team to validate cost/latency trade-offs in Dedicated and Hosted modes.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive deck with 6 scenarios and recommended procurement anchor points
Normalized benchmark CSV (latency, p95, cost-per-token, quantized-size, infra-affinity, license-type) uploaded to shared drive
Pilot checklist and 3 experiment definitions (synthetic load, real-traffic A/B, regional failover) reviewed by ENG and SRE
Stakeholder signoff from GTM lead and Head of Platform
updates: 2025-11-12: Kickoff meeting with GTM, SRE, Procurement; agreed on primary signals and acceptance criteria.
2025-11-20: Completed initial vendor list (14 candidates) and requested benchmark artifacts from Research.
2025-12-03: Research delivered normalized latency tables and token-cost estimates; discovered 2 vendors with non-standard licenses requiring legal review.
2025-12-15: Drafted scenario narratives and initial slide layout; asked Design to produce interactive mock for stakeholder walkthrough.
2026-01-07: Engineering provided synthetic load test scripts and preliminary runbook for region failover; estimate for infra tests added to plan.
2026-01-25: Legal flagged license-change shock scenario as high-risk; added mitigation language and procurement clause suggestions.
2026-02-10: Ran first field alpha probe with two model variants in eu-west; observed 18% higher p95 under 50% concurrent load than lab predictions.
2026-02-18: Deck iteration 2 ready; added cost sensitivity curves and canary rollback criteria following SRE feedback.
2026-02-28: Prepared materials for exec readout; awaiting final signoff meeting scheduled for 2026-03-03.
decisions: Prioritize scenarios that materially change procurement behavior: license shock, regional outage, and quantization incompatibility selected as primary triggers.
Use synthetic load + small real-traffic A/B for pilots rather than large bulk lab runs to surface p95 tails earlier.
Normalize cost to USD/1000 tokens and include a unit-cost delta band for decision anchors to simplify trade-offs in the deck.
tradeoffs: Depth vs breadth: limited to 14 vendors to maintain actionable detail; additional vendors will be an appendix and ongoing watchlist.
Speed vs accuracy: field alpha probes expose tail behavior quicker but require careful traffic shaping to avoid customer impact.
Operational complexity vs cost-savings: recommending hybrid routing increases infra complexity but can reduce unit cost by 12-25% for certain workloads.
next_steps: Finalize deck artifacts and circulate to Exec + Procurement by 2026-03-03
Schedule engineering spike to run the 3 experiment defs in dedicated staging (est. 2 sprints)
Request Legal to draft procurement clause language for license-change mitigation
Add 8 more vendors to the watchlist as a stretch deliverable if time remains
